analysis.title: GS SECTOR SPECIALISTS: Energy, Natural Resources and Utilities Preview: Three Things 16 Nov 2026
key_insights: Canadian Natural (CNQ) announced a deal to buy Advantage for about C$2.53B total value, against CNQ's market cap of C$144B. The desk does not expect it to shift the thesis for most US investors. CNQ keeps its target of returning 100% of free cash flow to shareholders through share repurchases.

The desk has seen elevated inbound interest in SMID-cap Canadian E&Ps for the last couple of months, with attention shifting from US small-cap E&Ps to Canadian names. It expects more questions on read-across to US names if Canadian consolidation continues, citing the recent premiums on announced CAD deals.

Advantage's October slide deck shows 86% of production tied to natural gas and 14% oil/liquids (2026E). Its three-year major infrastructure capital plan is largely complete, and 4Q2026 production was expected to hold through YE2027.

The desk thinks US hedge funds have been cautious on CNQ for most of the year because of wider WCS differentials, AECO natural gas exposure, and its willingness to do M&A. WCS bottomed at about $30 under and has been tightening from a very low base. With the crude flush, there is some debate about a flight to quality.
Names to watch after the CNQ deal: TOU, OVV, WCP, SDE.

Diamondback Energy (FANG) announced a core Midland Basin acquisition, buying Double Eagle units for $2.15B plus 15.56M shares. The desk says it was well telegraphed. The deal adds 176k net acres in the core of Midland, 68% undeveloped, and is described as leverage neutral, immediately accretive on cash flow per share and NAV per share, and valued at 4x 2027 EBITDA.

Diamondback also gave an early update on Barnett development, saying results exceed internal expectations for full field development and support momentum for full field development in 2027 and beyond.

The desk thinks specialists have been more cautious on FANG than on large-cap peers, where conversations on COP and DVN have been more positive recently. On GS numbers FANG trades at a 15% 2027 FCF yield versus 9% for EOG and 13% for OXY.

Per GS Futures desk (Rob Quinn), Commitment of Traders data through November 10 shows Managed Money selling of Brent futures remained sizeable after the US mid-term elections caused another leg lower in price. Net positioning fell below the 2-year median, and physical participants also liquidated. Discretionary strategies likely re-initiated longs afterward.
The Futures desk says a small hiccup in the diplomatic process could invigorate sidelined bulls. For now, larger CTA selling pressure has been avoided.

sector_views.rationale: Consolidation continues in Canada and the Permian. Cash generation is strong across E&Ps. The desk expects Canadian M&A to prompt read-across questions on US E&Ps.

earnings_insights: Diamondback's 3Q EPS shareholder letter said it expects to maintain consistent returns and that Permian upstream consolidation will continue at a more measured pace.
The desk cites strong cash generation across E&Ps as the reason it sees little concern over the CNQ deal's effect on its 100% FCF return target.
